subject: Cooking
title: Street Food and Climate Change
description: A short lesson to help you apply Street Food and Climate Change.

hook.text: Street food has a smaller carbon footprint than restaurant dining. But it faces climate threats of its own.

buildup.text: Charcoal — the fuel of most street food worldwide — contributes to deforestation and air pollution.

discovery.text: In Bangkok, street food contributes 14% of the city's particulate air pollution from cooking smoke.

twist.text: Solar cookers, LPG gas, and electric stalls are being tested as alternatives — cleaner but more expensive.

climax.text: Rising temperatures also threaten outdoor cooking — heat stress on vendors is a growing occupational hazard.

punchline.text: Street food must evolve to survive the climate it helped create.

quiz.question: What environmental challenge does charcoal-based street food cooking pose?

details.summary: Climate change threatens street food through rising temperatures that accelerate food spoilage, extreme weather that disrupts open-air vending, and supply chain disruptions that increase ingredient costs.
details.whyItMatters: Climate change disproportionately affects the 2.5 billion people who depend on street food daily. Protecting street food systems is a food security imperative as temperatures rise.
takeaways: Higher temperatures increase food spoilage risk for unrefrigerated vendors
Extreme weather events disrupt open-air vending for days or weeks
Supply chain disruptions from climate events raise ingredient costs

faq.question: How does rising temperature affect street food safety?
faq.answer: Higher ambient temperatures accelerate bacterial growth in food sitting at stalls without refrigeration. The danger zone of 40 to 140°F is reached faster and maintained longer. Food that was safe for six hours at 85°F may become unsafe in three hours at 100°F as tropical cities warm.

faq.question: What can be done to protect street food vendors from climate change?
faq.answer: Solar-powered portable refrigeration reduces spoilage. Covered vending structures protect from extreme heat and rain. Insurance programs for weather-related losses reduce financial vulnerability. Mobile payment systems help vendors track sales and reduce cash handling in wet conditions.
